summary:
Team NOVA SPACE LAB developed Lunar Landing Site Navigator, an interactive web application that unifies NASA Moon Trek OGC WMTS cartographic imagery (LRO WAC mosaics, LOLA elevation, shaded relief, slope, PSR, and Earth-visibility layers) with live NASA/JPL Horizons (DE441) topocentric ephemeris calculations in a South Polar Stereographic workspace (IAU2000:30120).

To support lunar South Pole exploration planning, users can inspect 17 categorized candidate regions—including Malapert Massif, Mons Mouton, and Connecting Ridge—or select custom coordinates south of 60°S across 24-hour, 7-day, and 30-day synodic UTC windows. The tool visualizes geometric solar elevation and sunlight percentages, direct-to-Earth (DTE) apparent disk visibility states, Earth-site range timelines, a local sky dome, unweighted side-by-side site comparisons, and provenance-tagged CSV exports.

Because the Sun and Earth hover near the South Pole horizon, illumination and DTE communication opportunities are tightly constrained. By pairing verifiable NASA/JPL data with transparent source credits and spherical-horizon boundaries, this Research & Educational Decision-Support Prototype (Not for Operational Certification) makes South Pole mission geometry accessible to educators, students, and analysts.
details:
Live Web App: https://lunar-landing-site-navigator-cb5d.vercel.app

Open-Source Repository: https://github.com/mhdshah000-cell/lunar-landing-site-navigator

1. What It Does & How It Works

Lunar Landing Site Navigator (by team NOVA SPACE LAB) is an interactive web application that pairs NASA Moon Trek OGC WMTS geospatial layers with live NASA/JPL Horizons (DE441) topocentric ephemeris calculations to explore geometric solar illumination and direct-to-Earth (DTE) line-of-sight visibility windows near the lunar South Pole.

- Interactive South Polar Stereographic Map (IAU2000:30120): Renders NASA Moon Trek WMTS tiles including the LRO WAC 100 m/px optical mosaic, LOLA 30 m/px elevation/shaded relief basemaps, and toggleable overlays for 18.6-year average Earth visibility, terrain slope (<=15 deg), and permanently shadowed regions (PSRs), paired with an interactive legend (units and transparency controls), polar graticule, live Sun/Earth azimuth vectors, and click-to-inspect custom coordinates south of 60 deg S.

- Categorized Candidate Site Directory (17 Locations): Separates NASA's October 28, 2024 refined 9 Artemis III regions (including Malapert Massif and Mons Mouton), 2022 Moon Trek 5 m/px study-box centers (including Connecting Ridge), and the IM-1 surface reference with coordinates, pole distances, and study-area dimensions.

- Live Topocentric Ephemeris & Time Controls: Evaluates 24-hour, 7-day, and 30-day synodic UTC windows (1900-2099) via a server-side proxy (/api/ephemeris) querying JPL Horizons DE441 (CENTER='coord@301', COORD_TYPE='GEODETIC', QUANTITIES='4,13,20'). Displays solar/Earth elevation and azimuth, 4-level apparent Earth disk clearance states (from target angular diameter), Earth-site range/rate, interactive SVG timelines with 15-minute scrubbing and animation, and a 0-20 deg Local Sky Dome.

- Two-Site Comparison, Provenance & Export: Provides side-by-side Location A vs. B solar/Earth comparison charts, an unweighted Quantitative Parameter Matrix, a dedicated Sources & Methods tab showing live service status, and provenance-tagged CSV exports.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

Because the Sun and Earth remain very close to the horizon at the lunar South Pole, surface illumination and DTE communication windows are narrow and time-sensitive. By uniting verified NASA cartography and JPL ephemeris geometry in an accessible browser workspace that requires no login, paywall, or visitor API key, this tool helps students, educators, researchers, and mission analysts inspect South Pole geometric trade-offs transparently.

3. Creativity & Factors Considered

- Strict Scientific Honesty: Distinguishes NASA/JPL sourced data, derived linear/crossing calculations, and explicit unavailable-data notices without ever fabricating fallback numbers.

- No Arbitrary Composite Scores: Site comparisons present unweighted physical parameters rather than invented rankings.

- Coordinate & Projection Integrity: Converts signed East/West coordinates to JPL's 0-360 deg East-positive MEAN_ME convention and clips raster layers cleanly to documented polar bounds.

- Responsive Cross-Device Access: Tested across desktop and mobile screen widths with server caching and retry/backoff handling for upstream NASA API traffic spikes.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Software & Hardware Used

- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, Vite, HTML5 Canvas, and interactive SVG visualizations.

- Backend & Deployment: Node.js, Express (server.ts), Vercel Serverless Functions (/api/ephemeris, /api/health), and Git/GitHub.

- Data Services: NASA/JPL Horizons REST API (DE441) and NASA Moon Trek OGC WMTS.

- Hardware: Standard desktop/laptop workstations and responsive mobile browsers.

5. Disclaimer & Scope

Research & Educational Decision-Support Prototype (Not for Operational Certification). This is an independent project and is not endorsed by NASA or JPL. All Sun and Earth horizon crossings are evaluated against an idealized 1,737.4 km spherical lunar horizon and do not perform local crater-rim DEM ray tracing, solar-array electrical power modeling, or RF link-budget / DSN scheduling certification.
